options.content: **Developer tier.** Every panel below the Memory Context row needs the exporter started with `--include-engula-debug-metrics` (off by default). If panels are empty, check that flag before anything else.

panels.description: Server memory from Valkey's own accounting: `zmalloc` is everything allocated, `logic` subtracts what maxmemory does not count, and `mutable_blocks` is the arena zone still being written into.
panels.title: Memory Used

panels.description: Arena memory Engula has identified as reclaimable but has not reclaimed yet.
panels.title: Memory Blocks

panels.description: Memory excluded from the maxmemory calculation — replication backlog, AOF buffers and client output buffers.
panels.title: Overhead

panels.description: How far logical memory usage sits above maxmemory, clamped at zero. Anything above zero is what eviction still has to recover.
panels.title: Memory To Free
Current Fill Rate
panels.description: Blocks grouped by how full they are, right now. Weight sitting in the low buckets is what defragmentation exists to compact. Series are labelled by bucket index: the server publishes 16 buckets and does not publish their boundaries.

panels.title: Fill Rate Over Time
panels.description: The same distribution over time, stacked. Weight migrating from the high buckets down to the low ones is fragmentation building up; the reverse is defragmentation winning.

panels.title: Block Population
panels.description: Blocks the arena is still writing into (`Mutable`) against blocks sealed and queued for reclamation (`Recycling`).

panels.title: Blocks per Task
panels.description: Blocks consumed and produced per completed defragmentation task. `After` staying well below `Before` is the compaction ratio each pass achieves.

panels.title: Task Creation
panels.description: Defragmentation tasks requested against tasks actually created. A gap between the two means requests are being rejected before a task exists.

panels.title: Task Skips
panels.description: Requests dropped without creating a task: `Threshold` when the block was not fragmented enough to be worth it, `Insufficient` when there was not enough material to build a task from.

panels.title: Inline Fallbacks
panels.description: Defragmentation done outside the background pipeline. `Main thread` work lands on the request path and shows up as latency; `Urgent` is the forced path taken under memory pressure.

panels.title: Blocks Selected per Task
panels.description: Blocks successfully picked up per created task — how much material each pass gets to work with.

panels.title: Blocks Retired vs Produced
panels.description: Blocks consumed and written back by completed tasks.

panels.title: Records Moved
panels.description: Records read out of retired blocks and written into new ones. The two should track each other — a lasting gap means records are being dropped or added along the way.

panels.title: Record Bytes Moved
panels.description: The same movement measured in bytes. `New` below `Old` is the space each pass squeezes out of the records it rewrites.

panels.title: Net Reclaimed
panels.description: Bytes retired minus bytes produced — what defragmentation actually gives back. Sustained time at or below zero means passes are running without recovering anything.

panels.title: Urgent Defrag Triggers
panels.description: What forced an urgent defragmentation pass: the eviction timer firing, or the eviction path hitting the memory wall inline.

panels.title: Evict Timer Starts
panels.description: How often the eviction timer is armed.

panels.title: Evict Timer Active
panels.description: Whether the eviction timer is currently armed (1) or idle (0).

panels.title: Forecast Keys
panels.description: Keys the eviction forecaster has walked.

title: Engula Defragmentation
description: Developer-tier view of Engula's defragmentation: which blocks are candidates, what the tasks do to them, and what triggers an urgent pass. Requires the exporter to run with --include-engula-debug-metrics.
